title: Alex O'Connor vs Dinesh D'Souza: Is the Bible True?
label: Bible truth and moral authority
motion: Is the Bible true in historical, moral, allegorical, theological, and revelatory senses, or do contradictions and morally troubling texts undermine its truth claims?
sourceNote: Assessment based exclusively on the complete locally cached YouTube caption transcript and timestamped events (transcript SHA-256 37c7f623340f7de14e1c23ac9ae897d13b0092e1a89147d49f06345b7a6e1e7f). Required below-high-confidence audio checks were completed before adjudication; representative quotations must be exact strings from quote-eligible locked source spans.
scoringNote: Scores are AI-generated estimates of argumentative performance under the locked adjudicated-consensus workflow. Repository code calculated every move, section, and overall result once, only after two isolated judgments, required audio review, and disputed-field adjudication closed.
summary: O'Connor pressed concrete historical and moral counterexamples, while D'Souza defended genre-sensitive revelation, cumulative testimony, moral development, and Christianity's beneficial interpretive traditions.

pro.text: The assertion that the universe had a beginning
pro.context: D'Souza identified several cosmological propositions in Genesis that he regarded as factual assertions open to examination through later inquiry.

con.text: Why why not this simple moral improvement?
con.context: O'Connor granted, for argument's sake, that immediate abolition might have been infeasible and asked why a narrower humane reform was absent.

sections.title: Standards of Truth, Genre, and Revelation

pro.words: Truth judgments should respect a work's genre and purpose, because incidental anachronisms or rearranged events need not defeat the deeper truth an author intends.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The Shakespeare analogy accepts the skeptic's genre-sensitive premise and develops it into a responsive account of how dramatic purpose, historical compression, and incidental inaccuracy can coexist with meaningful intended truth. Principal limitation: The reply never supplies a reliable criterion distinguishing an incidental rearrangement from a contradiction bearing directly upon the historical or theological purpose, leaving its protective boundary vulnerable to discretionary application. Live burden: The affirmative must classify the challenged Gospel details under a principled standard and show why their resolution is unnecessary, while still acknowledging that attempted historical reporting remains answerable to evidence. Locked score: The very strong band rewards direct central-burden contact, a coherent full answer, and fair engagement with genre sensitivity, while preserving substantial reservation about underdefined limits and only illustrative evidential support.

con.words: Because the Bible combines historical, allegorical, moral, theological, and metaphorical genres, each kind of truth claim requires evaluation under standards appropriate to that genre.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The library analogy establishes an intelligible, carefully differentiated framework for testing biblical claims, and the enumeration of distinct truth senses makes the governing proposition unusually recoverable, relevant, and appropriately qualified. Principal limitation: The Shakespeare comparison illustrates generic diversity effectively, but it leaves boundary cases underdeveloped, particularly texts combining theological purpose, purported history, literary shaping, and moral instruction within a single narrative presentation. Live burden: The skeptical case must consistently apply these genre-specific standards rather than treating every discrepancy alike, while explaining which historical, allegorical, or ethical failures genuinely undermine the broader motion-level claims under examination. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional coherence, direct central-burden contact, and disciplined scope, with only modest incompleteness concerning mixed genres and the precise consequences of failure within one truth category.

pro.words: Revelation addresses ultimate questions about purpose, death, and cosmic justice that unaided reason may not resolve, making faith a potentially reasonable mode of inquiry.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The move identifies several genuinely consequential questions and offers a clear positive rationale for why a revelatory framework might matter where ordinary empirical or philosophical methods have not delivered conclusive answers. Principal limitation: An inability of reason to settle a question neither establishes that revelation is necessary nor supplies evidence that a particular claimed revelation is reliable, accurate, or preferable to competing religious answers. Live burden: The affirmative must bridge epistemic limitation to warranted confidence in the Bible specifically, while distinguishing openness to faith from positive authentication of its theological, historical, and moral content. Locked score: The mixed band reflects substantial relevance and an intelligible motivation for revelation, but also materially overstated necessity, missing uncertainty, broad claims about reason's incapacity, and insufficient evidential movement toward biblical truth.

tags.label: Argument from ignorance
tags.context: The move risks inferring a need for reliable revelation from reason's inability to settle ultimate questions, without independently establishing the proposed revelatory source.

con.words: The Adam and Eve narrative retains serious allegorical tension because spiritual death does not straightforwardly explain expulsion from Eden or the guarded tree of life.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The argument anticipates the familiar spiritual-death interpretation and then identifies concrete narrative details, especially proactive banishment and the protected tree, that remain unexplained after granting that interpretive alternative. Principal limitation: Its criterion for successful allegorical coherence remains implicit, so the identified tension does not by itself demonstrate that every theological or symbolic reading of the narrative must be deficient. Live burden: The skeptical side must show why these unresolved details damage the relevant allegorical or theological truth claim, while the affirmative side must connect mortality, expulsion, and the tree through a principled interpretation. Locked score: The very strong band recognizes precise textual engagement, substantial charity, and a proportionately qualified conclusion, while reserving room because the governing standard of allegorical adequacy and the motion-level consequence receive limited development.

pro.words: Ancient Gospel reports should be judged under human historical conventions that permit collected testimony, narrative compression, and minor discrepancies without automatically defeating reliability.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The reply productively distinguishes ancient historiographical practice from anachronistic expectations, directly explaining why mediated testimony, narrative compression, and limited divergence need not automatically extinguish historical credibility. Principal limitation: That reminder remains insufficient, because toleration of non-eyewitness compilation or imprecision cannot independently authenticate particular accounts, reconcile concrete contradictions, or resolve documented editorial and oral transmission problems. Live burden: The defense must articulate a discriminating ancient-reporting criterion, apply it to the itinerary, dating, and instruction conflicts, and demonstrate why transmission alterations do not undermine reliability. Locked score: The mixed 65–74 band appropriately recognizes central relevance and responsiveness while withholding credit for unstable terminology, absent qualification, incomplete transmission contact, and a warrant that exceeds the evidence presented.

con.words: Conflicting Gospel accounts of Passover timing, permitted equipment, temple chronology, and Mary Magdalene's knowledge weaken the narratives' historical reliability.
con.critique: Strongest feature: O'Connor distinguishes divergent testimony from incompatible particulars, then anchors the reliability challenge in disputes about Passover chronology, missionary equipment, temple sequencing, and Magdalene's epistemic position. Principal limitation: Although this enumeration establishes localized inconsistency with exceptional specificity, the probabilistic transition from several contradictions to diminished historical reliability remains underarticulated, especially concerning independence, provenance, harmonization criteria, and differential evidential significance. Live burden: The affirmative must demonstrate coherent reconciliations preserving linguistic meaning and chronological integrity, while the negative must explain why these discrepancies substantially undermine testimony rather than merely peripheral inerrancy. Locked score: The very strong 91 reflects outstanding precision, calibration, charity, and burden relevance, with the incompletely quantified reliability inference restraining a formidable constructive contribution.

pro.words: The four nonidentical Gospels should be weighed cumulatively like testimony, with awkward details such as women discovering the empty tomb potentially supporting authenticity.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The cumulative-testimony model directly addresses how nonidentical accounts might retain evidential force, and the appeal to culturally awkward witnesses supplies a concrete, potentially relevant marker rather than mere assertion. Principal limitation: The jury analogy understates dependence among sources, theological selection, transmission history, and the possibility that vivid or awkward details can arise without independently confirming the narrated event. Live burden: The affirmative must establish relevant independence and explain why the cited features discriminate authenticity from literary or communal development, while answering the distinct editing challenge rather than treating all variation as corroboration. Locked score: The mixed band recognizes central relevance, a recoverable evidential proposal, and partial responsiveness, but reflects overstated confidence, limited comparative warrant, inadequate qualification, and failure to resolve the strongest source-dependence and transmission objections.

tags.label: Subjective validation
tags.context: The personal impression that Mark has a ring of authenticity carries more argumentative weight than the supplied comparative evidence can support.

con.words: Documented interpolations and variant Gospel endings establish later editing and make alteration during preceding oral transmission plausible, thereby reducing confidence in historical reliability.
con.critique: Strongest feature: O'Connor anchors the transmission challenge in manuscript phenomena, particularly Mark's discrepant endings, then advances the proportionate inference that comparable reshaping during undocumented oral circulation remains plausible. Principal limitation: Observable postcomposition interpolation does not establish precomposition alteration, and the argument underdevelops whether identification of late variants evidences textual comparison, circumscribed contamination, or generalized unreliability. Live burden: D'Souza must explain why recoverable written editing provides little evidential purchase on less recoverable oral development, while O'Connor must connect possibility to meaningful probability without treating every tradition as equally unstable. Locked score: The very strong 85–94 band appropriately reflects a precise, centrally relevant evidential challenge whose calibrated modal conclusion survives, notwithstanding an inferential bridge that remains suggestive rather than demonstrative.

pro.words: Genesis asserts that the universe began, came from nothing in a qualified sense, and was created by God, offering cosmological claims for later examination.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The move clearly separates three propositions attributed to Genesis and correctly frames them as factual assertions made by the text, thereby creating a testable subsidiary route rather than relying exclusively upon symbolism. Principal limitation: The phrase concerning emergence from nothing remains imprecise, and identifying claims that later inquiry can examine does not establish either scientific anticipation or the specifically theological proposition that divine creation occurred. Live burden: The affirmative must provide independent evidence connecting cosmological findings to Genesis rather than merely noting verbal resemblance, while answering alternative interpretations of beginnings, creation, and nothingness. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects clear recoverability, coherent enumeration, and useful supporting relevance, while recognizing limited evidential completion, terminological looseness, and the distance between a cosmic beginning and revelation by God.

con.words: Counting Genesis as scientifically informative when cosmology appears favorable, but non-scientific when its earth-sun sequence conflicts with observation, applies inconsistent standards.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The reply diagnoses a precise methodological inconsistency by juxtaposing favorable cosmological treatment with unfavorable creation-order evidence, then demands a principled basis for assigning different evidential significance to each passage. Principal limitation: The criticism depends upon accurately fixing the affirmative's interpretive commitments, and it leaves open whether broad origin claims and detailed narrative sequencing could legitimately serve different literary purposes without inconsistency. Live burden: The affirmative must articulate a textually grounded distinction that was not invented merely to preserve agreement, while the skeptic must show that both claims were actually offered under comparable scientific standards. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional responsiveness, stable terminology, sharp logical structure, and an effective diagnostic challenge, with modest reservation because a defensible genre distinction remains conceptually available if independently supported.

pro.words: Biblical descriptions associated with David's palace and Sodom and Gomorrah can guide archaeological inquiry and support limited historical or geographical informational value.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The reply supplies concrete archaeological illustrations and a coherent reason to regard biblical descriptions as potentially productive historical-geographical guides, thereby giving the corroboration case substance. Principal limitation: Locational correspondence for David’s palace or proposed sites associated with Sodom and Gomorrah cannot independently establish broader narrative reliability, and the argument leaves that generalizing bridge materially compressed, implicitly qualified, and slightly overstated. Live burden: Because the decisive objection concerns whether favorable and unfavorable evidence receive consistent inferential treatment, these examples remain relevant contrary material but do not answer the selectivity diagnosis or vindicate central miraculous claims. Locked score: The strong/competent result reflects excellent central-burden relevance and solid coherence, evidence, and clarity, while withholding greater credit for unacknowledged uncertainty, restricted corroborative reach, and incomplete responsiveness to the targeted methodological criticism.

con.words: Logical possibility removes an impossibility objection but supplies no evidence that a biblical miracle occurred and applies equally to competing religious miracle reports.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The reply precisely separates logical possibility from evidential support for actual occurrence, then uses symmetrical comparison with a rival religious miracle to expose the modal mistake and its discriminatory consequence. Principal limitation: Although nearly complete as a diagnostic rebuttal, it does not independently evaluate the quality of the underlying Gospel testimony, so its conclusion defeats possibility as positive support without settling every cumulative historical consideration. Live burden: The pro side must therefore explain how resurrection reports gain event-specific evidential weight after impossibility is conceded, while supplying a principled standard that would not comparably authenticate Muhammad’s reported ascent or other competing miracle traditions. Locked score: The very-strong result recognizes exceptional coherence, precision, responsiveness, calibration, and charity, with restraint reflecting the subsidiary burden tier and bounded reach beyond modal diagnosis.

sections.title: Divine Violence and Biblical Moral Authority

pro.words: The Bible develops from Old Testament retaliation toward New Testament forgiveness, with fulfillment understood as moral transcendence rather than simple repetition of earlier practices.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly engages the central objection by tracing an intelligible movement from retaliation toward forgiveness, while fulfillment as transcendence provides a coherent mechanism connecting the testaments rather than merely juxtaposing them. Principal limitation: This developmental contrast supplies no principled criterion distinguishing legitimate accommodation from defective authorization, so later ethical improvement cannot retrospectively vindicate earlier commands or demonstrate their moral truth. Live burden: The pro side must explain why an omnibenevolent authority permitted the challenged violence initially, while showing that transcendence preserves biblical authority instead of conceding consequential correction within the tradition. Locked score: This strong, highly relevant answer achieves substantial dialectical contact and recognizable evidential support, but imprecise qualification, overstated warrant, and incomplete engagement with the earlier killings appropriately prevent a very-strong assessment.

con.words: Divinely ordered conquest, plunder, forced labor, and killing involving Amalekite children and animals directly challenge the Old Testament's asserted moral authority.
con.critique: Strongest feature: O'Connor formulates a concrete, proposition-level moral counterexample: divinely commanded conquest, plunder, forced labor, and indiscriminate destruction, especially children and animals, appear straightforwardly incompatible with the Old Testament's moral authority. Principal limitation: The excerpt establishes the intuitive contradiction but underdevelops the interpretive, historical, and metaethical premises needed to exclude divine-judgment defenses, beyond demonstrating their moral repugnance. Live burden: D'Souza must explain, without presupposing divine goodness or redescribing innocence away, how killing children and animals can constitute authoritative judgment, while O'Connor must defend reliability and applicability of the moral intuition grounding his challenge. Locked score: The very strong 85–94 band fits direct motion-level relevance, stable scope, explicit dilemma, and formidable burden placement, with restraint for compressed rival hermeneutics.

pro.words: Christian tradition developed restraints upon killing women and children, and later condemnation of civilian slaughter draws meaningfully upon that inherited moral framework.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The appeal to just-war restraint provides relevant evidence that Christian moral development produced consequential principles against targeting women and children, thereby supporting the affirmative's broader tradition-based moral route. Principal limitation: Sweeping claims that nobody before Christianity recognized such restraints and that everybody subsequently violated them are unsupported, historically overbroad, and irrelevant to whether earlier biblical conquest commands were morally justified. Live burden: The affirmative must establish influence without claiming exclusive moral authorship and must connect later restraint to the original textual problem, while allowing that comparable principles may arise independently. Locked score: The weak band reflects significant central relevance and a recognizable historical contribution, but also severe overstatement, limited warrant, poor representation of alternatives, and a relevant nonanswer to the decisive challenge concerning divinely ordered noncombatant killing.

tags.label: Scope neglect
tags.context: The move treats broad claims about all pre-Christian and contemporary warfare without evidence proportionate to their historical and geographical scope.

con.words: Later New Testament moral development cannot retroactively change the moral status of earlier divine commands involving defeated combatants, women, children, and animals.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The reply isolates the temporal gap between later moral improvement and earlier justification, then grounds that diagnosis in a concrete conquest sequence involving combatants driven away and noncombatants left behind. Principal limitation: It assumes the relevant narrative straightforwardly attributes morally authoritative divine command and does not extensively consider literary, hyperbolic, judgment-based, or human-misattribution interpretations that might alter the target proposition. Live burden: The affirmative must explain the original command's status rather than citing later restraint, while the skeptic must defend the textual attribution and moral characterization underlying the counterexample. Locked score: The very strong band follows from exceptional coherence, direct diagnostic responsiveness, concrete warrant, and unusually charitable isolation of what progressive revelation can and cannot establish, with only limited interpretive premises left comparatively compressed.

sections.title: Slavery, Moral Development, and Abolitionist Reception

pro.words: Quaker and evangelical abolitionism demonstrates that Christian reading of the Bible can motivate opposition to slavery rather than functioning only as its defense.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The reply supplies concrete, consequential evidence: Quaker and evangelical abolitionists read the same biblical canon as authorizing resistance to slavery, defeating any contention that Christian scripture functions only as oppression's ideological instrument. Principal limitation: This counterexample concerns communal appropriation rather than the criticized law's morality, and neither explains why that law omitted preserving an enslaved family nor establishes abolitionism's predominance over proslavery reception. Live burden: The argument must connect the liberatory tradition to the text, explain its treatment of the troubling provision, and show why beneficial reception outweighs contrary uses. Locked score: The strong/competent 76 recognizes substantial historical support, central relevance, and coherent limited force while retaining deductions for nonresponse, implicit qualification, and incomplete representational charity.

con.words: Biblical slave law separated released men from enslaved wives and children and imposed unequal lifelong bondage despite an available, modest humane reform.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The reply isolates a modest reform in biblical slave law, granting immediate abolition might have been infeasible while showing that family release required minimal institutional disruption. Principal limitation: Although powerful against incremental-development reasoning, it remains partial because it does not contact the distinct claim about later Christian restraints on warfare, and its evidence concerns a specified legal disparity rather than comprehensive theology. Live burden: The pro side must explain why a morally authoritative legislator omitted this narrowly humane protection and imposed unequal lifelong bondage, without invoking feasibility considerations that the family-release proposal specifically circumvents. Locked score: Exceptional coherence, precision, calibration, and representational charity make this a very strong central counterexample, while its bounded scope and unaddressed adjacent target appropriately keep it below the highest band.

pro.words: Established communal reading and moral use shape textual significance, and the long abolitionist reception of Exodus weighs against an exclusively oppression-supporting interpretation.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The reply presents reception evidence—enslaved readers, abolitionist preachers, and Martin Luther King—and establishes that Exodus acquired liberatory significance within communities, challenging interpretations treating oppressive content as its exhaustive meaning. Principal limitation: It slides from the proposition that communal use contributes to significance toward the proposition that use determines significance, without comparing rival traditions or explaining how emancipationist appropriation changes objectionable commands' morality. Live burden: The argument must distinguish meaning, significance, and moral status, justify liberatory reception's authority, and address the slave-law omission and genocide objection. Locked score: The mixed 74 credits relevant historical evidence and a partial answer, while reflecting overstated calibration, unstable scope, incomplete responsiveness, and reduced charity toward coexisting beneficial use and harmful content.

tags.label: Equivocation
tags.context: The argument moves between significance as one dimension shaped by reception and significance as something determined by reception, materially strengthening the conclusion without defending that shift.

con.words: Old Testament permission of slavery and New Testament obedience to cruel masters leave canonical moral instability even if some other passage opposed slavery.
con.critique: Strongest feature: O'Connor juxtaposes Old Testament authorization with New Testament obedience to cruel masters, exposing why abolitionist reception and liberatory appropriation cannot establish a consistently anti-slavery canon. Principal limitation: The reply establishes textual moral instability, but does not fully defeat a developmental canonical hierarchy treating permissive rules as historically accommodated constraints subordinated to later emancipatory principles. Live burden: D'Souza must justify that hierarchy without merely appealing to beneficial reception, explaining why divinely presented law permits human ownership and why apostolic instruction demands obedience under cruelty while still warranting coherent moral authority. Locked score: Exceptionally direct diagnostic contact, an explicit hypothetical concession, stable scope, proportionate force, and substantial contrary textual evidence justify the very-strong 93, while the unresolved developmental-reading possibility appropriately prevents a higher assessment.

strengths: Established a useful genre-and-purpose framework that accepted the need for differentiated truth standards while explaining why some literary rearrangement may be incidental.
Identified clear cosmological propositions in Genesis and offered archaeological and reception-based evidence rather than relying exclusively on abstract theology.
Presented a coherent canonical-development thesis linking fulfillment, forgiveness, just-war restraint, and abolitionist appropriation within Christian moral tradition.
Engaged Gospel reliability through ancient reporting conventions and a cumulative-testimony model, giving the historical case an identifiable evidential structure.

blunders.text: The case repeatedly moved from possibility, useful reception, or local corroboration toward broader reliability without supplying discriminating evidence or sufficiently principled limits.
Later Christian moral development and beneficial abolitionist use did not answer why earlier conquest and slave provisions attributed to divine authority were morally permissible.
Several historically sweeping claims about Christianity's exclusive role in restraining warfare exceeded the evidence and weakened an otherwise relevant tradition-based defense.

strengths: Established the debate's governing genre-sensitive standard and applied it through concrete historical, allegorical, scientific, and moral tests.
Presented specific Gospel contradictions and transmission variants while carefully distinguishing demonstrated editing from merely plausible earlier alteration.
Diagnosed the difference between logical possibility and occurrence evidence with a symmetrical rival-religion example.
Pressed exceptionally concrete moral counterexamples involving conquest, family separation, lifelong bondage, and obedience to cruel masters.

Granted major affirmative alternatives, including spiritual death, progressive revelation, infeasibility of immediate abolition, and hypothetical antislavery passages, before identifying their remaining burdens.

blunders.text: The skeptical case sometimes left the exact motion-level consequence implicit, showing a serious failure within one truth category without fully specifying how far that failure generalized across the biblical library.
Some textual challenges could have more fully developed their legal, literary, and canonical contexts, especially where alternative genre or accommodation accounts remained available.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that biblical truth is best defended as a layered revelatory claim whose historical, literary, and moral components require distinct warrants, cumulative evaluation, and a principled account of development.
premises: Genre sensitivity must be constrained by publicly stated criteria: details are incidental only when they neither carry the narrative's asserted historical conclusion nor determine its theological interpretation.

Cumulative Gospel testimony has force only after accounting for literary dependence, editorial purpose, manuscript variation, and the difference between shared tradition and genuinely independent attestation.

Cosmological and archaeological correspondences provide limited corroboration, not direct proof of revelation, and their value depends upon applying the same interpretive standard to favorable and unfavorable details.

Moral development can preserve biblical authority only if earlier troubling commands are treated through a defensible account of accommodation, fallible human attribution, or bounded judgment rather than justified merely by later improvement.
finalArgument.conclusion: Accordingly, a proportionate affirmative conclusion is that the Bible may remain a credible vehicle of revelation if its central claims survive genre-specific testing and its moral development receives a principled, non-evasive interpretation.

newArguments.title: Constrained critical realism
newArguments.text: A stronger affirmative model would treat inspiration as compatible with identifiable human limitation while refusing to use that compatibility as an unrestricted escape. Historical claims remain corrigible and must face ordinary source criticism; theological claims are assessed for coherence and explanatory reach; moral texts are evaluated within an explicit developmental framework. This model gains credibility when it predicts where literary shaping should appear and identifies in advance which central claims could not be surrendered without changing Christianity's substance.

newArguments.title: Reception as defeasible evidence
newArguments.text: Abolitionist and liberatory reception should be offered as defeasible evidence about a canon's moral affordances, not as a verdict erasing contrary provisions. If sustained communities can derive equality, deliverance, and restraint through recognizable textual principles, that history supports the claim that those principles are genuinely present. The defense becomes stronger when it also acknowledges proslavery reception, explains why its interpretive method is inferior, and identifies canonical rules that consistently prioritize liberation over accommodation.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that biblical truth claims deserve genre-specific assessment, but attempted history, divine moral authority, and revelation remain undermined when concrete conflicts survive the strongest principled harmonization.
premises: A discrepancy matters historically when competing accounts assert incompatible facts and the conflict bears upon chronology, instruction, identity, causation, or another feature the narrative presents as reportable.
Known textual editing does not prove pervasive corruption, but it raises a targeted reliability concern wherever a central tradition lacks early, independent, and comparatively stable attestation.

The possibility of divine action removes only an impossibility objection; positive belief in a particular miracle still requires evidence that discriminates it from error, legend, symbolism, and rival religious testimony.

A developmental moral reading remains inadequate unless it explains why earlier commands attributed to a perfectly good authority were permissible then, misattributed by human authors, or represented through a nonliteral genre.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore, skepticism is warranted toward the Bible's stronger historical, revelatory, and moral-authority claims wherever unresolved contradictions, nondiscriminating miracle arguments, or unexplained divine commands remain after genre-sensitive analysis.

newArguments.title: Failure propagation by claim type
newArguments.text: The skeptical case can avoid overgeneralization by mapping each failure to the claim it directly affects. A chronological contradiction weakens a historical report; a selective scientific reading weakens an argument for prescience; an unexplained command to kill noncombatants weakens perfect moral authorship. Several independent failures may cumulatively challenge a broader doctrine of revelation, but only after an explicit bridge explains why that doctrine predicts reliable performance across those particular domains.

newArguments.title: Symmetrical interpretive discipline
newArguments.text: A robust skeptical method should announce its interpretive rules before examining favorable or unfavorable passages. The same standards for genre, hyperbole, textual development, source dependence, and moral accommodation must govern both apparent successes and apparent failures. This symmetry answers the concern that skepticism simply prefers troublesome readings, while also sharpening the criticism of defenses that classify a passage as factual when it resembles modern knowledge but poetic when its sequence conflicts with observation.
